scope: Read-only plausibility review of staged ShadeBalancePass.cs against native iteration03 evidence and the current saved scene. No app input, scene mutation, rendered candidate or final lighting score.
visualBasis: At hour16 the crate front, reinforcement and painted surface collapse toward a common dark value despite retained mapping. Its placement and form remain readable, but material separation is weaker than at noon.
The hour16 canopy underside is nearly black outside a strong warm practical-light patch. This prevents a useful close judgment of cloth wear and exaggerates the angular appearance of some folds.

At noon the underside is already a broad, dark, largely featureless red surface. The staged afternoon-only key change cannot resolve this noon issue. New cloth binding should be inspected under the unchanged noon lighting before deciding whether an additional illumination change is needed.

curveScope.actualInterpolatedInfluence: 12 < hour < 19, because the existing smoothstep interpolation blends the modified 17.5 key with the retained noon and 19 keys.
curveScope.noonAndNight: Noon and times at/after19 through the unchanged overnight/morning keys retain their previous frame values.
curveScope.interpretation: The stronger cool sky and warm ground/equator are a reasonable controlled audition for readable late-day shade. These numbers are not rendered proof or an appearance approval.

practicalLightInvestigation.sourceStateCaveat: These are current saved-scene values, not a fresh runtime diagnostic of the immutable iteration03 build. The staged pass does not modify this light.
practicalLightInvestigation.name: Lamp warm Finery entrance light
practicalLightInvestigation.conclusion: A close omnidirectional practical plausibly produces the concentrated warm underside patch. A point light has no spotlight cone edge, so the angular bands cannot be diagnosed as a cone cutoff. Fold normals, self-shadowing and bias remain possible contributors; no geometry hole or shadow bug is established by this read-only evidence. Ambient adjustment leaves the source of the patch intact.

fillInvestigation.inference: It shines downward and mainly assists suitably oriented exterior faces. Raising its intensity alone is not a physical lower-hemisphere bounce solution for downward-facing cloth. Because it has no shadows, excessive strength can also flatten covered recesses.

boundedNativeChecks: Compare the same crate, trash, scrap-back, canopy-top, canopy-under and reference-wide cameras at noon,16,17.5,18.25 and night. Include18.25 because the revised key also influences the approach to19.

Require readable material differences in shade while sunlit stone and metal retain their existing exposure and the warm sun/cool shade distinction. Check dark joints, handle cavities and prop/ground contact for loss of depth from broad ambient and unshadowed fill.

Inspect the canopy underside with the actual new cloth maps at unchanged noon. Do not bake light into color, lift cloth into emission, or exaggerate normal/texture contrast to conceal insufficient illumination.

At16 and night inspect the close lamp patch in successive native frames. If hard angular bands persist, use an isolated operator-controlled lamp-shadow comparison to separate shadow behavior from surface normals before changing geometry or broad scene lighting.
Reconfirm actual reflection capture completion after time changes. The pass preserves reflection strength but updated ambient/fill can still alter captured content.
